name: Meta AI-enabled coding interview
citation: Primary report: Jason Koebler, 'Meta Is Going to Let Job Candidates Use AI During Coding Tests', 404 Media, 29 Jul 2025, https://www.404media.co/meta-is-going-to-let-job-candidates-use-ai-during-coding-tests/ (paywalled after the opening). Confirmation: Sarah Jackson, 'Meta will let some job candidates use AI in their coding interviews', Business Insider, 29 Jul 2025 (syndicated at https://www.aol.com/meta-let-job-candidates-ai-160303820.html). Secondary: Craig Hale, 'Meta says it will let candidates use AI in some job interviews', TechRadar Pro, 30 Jul 2025, https://www.techradar.com/pro/meta-is-going-to-let-candidates-use-ai-in-job-interviews. Later primary Meta statement: Meta Careers, 'Hiring process' page (FAQ and interviewing note, undated, read Nov 2026), https://www.metacareers.com/hiring-process/. Wired: [uncertain] a Wired version is referenced by search summaries and a #wired-tagged social post, but no Wired URL was located and wired.com could not be fetched.
evidence_tier: Secondary press reporting a leaked internal company post (404 Media, Business Insider with Meta confirmation and spokesperson quote); plus a later primary company statement (Meta Careers hiring-process page). Format specifics (60 minutes, replaces one onsite coding round, October 2025 pilot start) come only from practitioner/vendor blogs.
access_status: 404 Media: opening paragraphs only, rest paywalled. Business Insider (via AOL): fully read in summarised form. TechRadar: fully read. Meta Careers hiring-process page: fully read. interviewing.io blog: fully read. Wired: not accessed (domain blocked to the fetcher; no article URL found).
sponsor_and_incentive: Meta is the hiring company and is investing heavily in AI coding tools and models (Llama), so it has an incentive to frame AI use as the normal working environment. 404 Media and Business Insider are independent press. CoderPad (interview platform hosting the AI assistant) and interview-prep firms (interviewing.io, Hello Interview, Prepfully, Exponent) sell products tied to this format and publish most of the format detail.
exact_quotes: Internal Meta post, as quoted by Business Insider (AOL syndication): "Meta is developing a new type of coding interview in which candidates have access to an AI assistant." Same post (visible opening of 404 Media; also Business Insider, TechRadar): "This is more representative of the developer environment that our future employees will work in." Same post, fragment as quoted by TechRadar: "makes LLM-based cheating less effective"; fuller sentence reported in search snippets of Business Insider NL as "...more representative of the developer environment that our future employees will work in, and also makes LLM-based cheating less effective" [uncertain: full sentence not seen in an opened source]. Internal post (Business Insider): "The questions are still in development; data from you will help shape the future of interviewing at Meta." Post title per secondary coverage: "AI-Enabled Interviews - Call for Mock Candidates" [uncertain]. 404 Media visible text: employees asked to volunteer for a "mock AI-enabled interview." Meta spokesperson to Business Insider: "We're obviously focused on using AI to help engineers with their day-to-day work." and "Humans talking to humans will always be part of the interview process, that remains unchanged." Meta Careers hiring-process page, Interviewing section: "Select roles now include an authorized AI assistant within CoderPad during technical interviews." FAQ: "Yes, many of Meta's interviews now include an AI assistant built into the interview environment." "Candidates are expected to use this AI assistant as part of the interview." "Practicing with AI coding tools and being comfortable reading, debugging, and building on existing code will help you feel prepared." "Candidates use the built-in AI assistant in CoderPad, which includes Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Meta's models." "No outside AI tools or assistance are authorized - only the tools available within the interview environment may be used." FAQ also says the interviews aim to evaluate "the problem-solving, coding, debugging, and collaboration skills" needed for software engineers at Meta.
date_and_recency: 404 Media and Business Insider: 29 Jul 2025; TechRadar 30 Jul 2025. Internal post reportedly from early July 2025 [uncertain]. Pilot start October 2025 per interviewing.io only [uncertain]. Meta Careers page is undated; read 21 Nov 2026 and lists Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta models as available in CoderPad (specific model versions not stated by Meta; blog lists such as GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4/4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Llama 4 Maverick are [uncertain]).
key_claims: 1) In July 2025 Meta told employees, in an internal post, it was developing a coding interview in which candidates have access to an AI assistant, and asked staff to sit mock AI-enabled interviews to help shape the questions. 2) Meta's stated rationale in that post was that the format is more representative of the developer environment future employees will work in and makes LLM-based cheating less effective. 3) Meta confirmed the move to Business Insider; its spokesperson tied it to Meta's focus on using AI to help engineers in their daily work and said humans talking to humans remains part of the process. 4) By late 2026 Meta's own careers page states that select roles, and many interviews, include an authorized AI assistant in CoderPad, that candidates are expected to use it, that design interviews use the same assistant with Mermaid Markdown, and that outside AI tools are banned. 5) Practitioner blogs claim the round began as a pilot in October 2025, runs 60 minutes, and replaces one of two onsite coding rounds [uncertain].
headline_figures: No quantitative data published by Meta. Format numbers from blogs only: 60-minute round; replaces one of the two onsite coding rounds; pilot began October 2025 (interviewing.io, Githire Wahome, undated c. 2026) [uncertain]. No pass rates, candidate counts or validity figures disclosed.
sample_and_method: Not a study. News reporting based on internal Meta communications seen by 404 Media, confirmed by Meta to Business Insider. Meta recruited current employees as mock candidates to trial the questions; no numbers or results disclosed. Subjects are software engineering candidates.
what_is_measured: Per Meta Careers: problem-solving, coding, debugging and collaboration skills for software engineers, with preparation advice stressing reading, debugging and building on existing code with AI tools. Implicitly includes tool fluency in directing an AI assistant. Blogs say interviewers judge how well candidates leverage the AI without using it as a crutch, and list criteria such as problem solving, code quality, verification and communication [uncertain].
ai_policy_in_interview: Permitted, and per the later Meta Careers page expected: an in-environment AI assistant (CoderPad, choice of Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Meta models). Outside AI tools are banned. Earlier prep materials reportedly said AI use was optional with no bearing on outcome [uncertain].
scope_and_status: July 2025: in development, trialled internally with employee mock candidates; 'some' coding candidates. Late 2026 (Meta Careers): 'select roles' and 'many' technical interviews include the assistant, including design interviews. Blogs say it started as an invite-only pilot in October 2025 for back-end and ops-focused SWE roles, likely extending to all SWE roles in 2026 [uncertain].
validity_evidence: None published. Meta has disclosed no criterion-validity data (correlation with job performance) for the AI-enabled format or for the traditional format it replaces.
relevance_to_angle: Supports 'working with an agent' and 'basic fluency': a major employer redesigned a coding round around directing an AI assistant and now expects candidates to use it, explicitly to mirror real work. Supports moving away from pure convergent coding, since prep guidance emphasises reading, debugging and extending existing code. Complicates the angle in that the round is still a timed, individual coding exercise in CoderPad, not a design conversation or team-fit assessment, and the stated anti-cheating motive shows the redesign is partly defensive rather than purely about better measurement.
limitations_stated: Internal post: "The questions are still in development; data from you will help shape the future of interviewing at Meta." Coverage described it as applying to 'some' candidates. Meta Careers limits it to "Select roles". Prep blogs note Meta had not formally published a full guide, so format details are unofficial.
counter_evidence: Peers moved the other way at the time: Business Insider reports Amazon told recruiters to disqualify applicants found using AI in interviews, and Anthropic initially barred AI in applications before reversing. No evidence the format predicts job performance better than the old one. interviewing.io's author says candidates may get an underpowered model and that the 'optional' framing was not true in practice [uncertain], which suggests the measured skill may be partly tool-specific. The anti-cheating rationale implies the format is also a response to cheating, not only a better construct.
verification_status: Verified against opened sources: 404 Media headline, author, date and the 'more representative of the developer environment' quote (visible opening); Business Insider quotes from the internal post and spokesperson (AOL syndication); TechRadar fragment 'makes LLM-based cheating less effective'; all Meta Careers quotes. [uncertain]: full combined sentence with the cheating clause (only in search snippets of Business Insider NL); post title 'Call for Mock Candidates'; early-July internal post date; any Wired corroboration (not opened); October 2025 pilot start, 60-minute length, replacement of one onsite round, role scope and model versions (blogs only). Re-checked 2026-11-21 by fetching https://www.metacareers.com/hiring-process/ directly (HTTP 200): the sentences 'Candidates are expected to use this AI assistant as part of the interview.', 'many of Meta's interviews now include an AI assistant' and 'Select roles now include an authorized AI assistant within CoderPad during technical interviews.' are present verbatim. The page shows no date.
